lines.trans: Smell the skin of this lemon, Qing—like sunshine after rain!
How many kilos do we need for Friday's tarts and hot tea?
Three kilos of lemons and two big glass jars of flower honey.
Good morning! Need an extra pair of arms for those heavy jars?
Peng! You found the neighbourhood market already!
I grew up three streets from this square—nothing smells better on Saturday.
Taste a spoon of this dark mountain honey, Peng. Is it too sweet?
Not at all—warm and rich, just like my mother bought in autumn.

words.gloss: at all (一点也不 not at all)

lines.trans: Two big jars and three kilos of lemons, paid in cash with coins to spare!
Give me the heavy basket with the glass jars; you take the herbs.
Next stop: the pottery table at the corner for twelve white teacups!
Lead the way, Mei—we are ahead of budget already!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yī. Changes tone to yí before 4th tone (一个 yí gè) and yì before 1st/2nd/3rd tones (一杯 yì bēi).

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yí yàng. Pairs with 跟/和 in 跟…一样 ('the same as…').

examples.text: 等等，深蓝色的，跟您的一样啊！
examples.trans: Wait—it is dark blue, the same as yours!

examples.text: 哎呀！我跑得太急，包装看着都一样！
examples.trans: Oh no! I was running in such a rush that the wrappers all looked alike!

meanings.en: completely identical; cast from the same mold
meanings.note: Pinyin: yì mú yí yàng. Note second-tone mú here ('one mold, one look').

examples.text: 外面一模一样，可是你看里面！
examples.trans: The outside is identical, yet look inside!

examples.text: 咬一口……志豪，闭上眼睛！跟梧桐巷的味道一模一样！
examples.trans: One bite... Zhihao, close your eyes! It tastes identical to Wutong Lane!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yì diǎn. Before a noun, means 'a little bit of' (一点糖); after an adjective, 'a bit more' (快一点).

examples.text: 只有一点点牛奶、两个鸡蛋，一点黄油都没有！
examples.trans: Only a tiny bit of milk, two eggs, and no butter at all!

examples.text: 太好了！请加牛奶和一点糖。
examples.trans: Wonderful! With milk and a little sugar, please.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sān. Cardinal number 3; combines with measure words (三个) and floors (三楼).

examples.text: 不在，只有我的笔和三张旧收据！
examples.trans: Not there—only my pen and three old receipts!

examples.text: 三瓶牛奶、二十个鸡蛋、黄油、奶酪和红苹果！
examples.trans: Three bottles of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià. Used for downward motion ('go down'), location ('under'), or 'next' (下周).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià cì. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 下一次 ('the next occasion').

examples.text: 下次来成都，一定再来住我们客栈！
examples.trans: Next time you come to Chengdu, be sure to stay at our inn again!

examples.text: 今天聊得很开心，我们下次见！
examples.trans: It was lovely chatting today—see you next time!

meanings.note: Pinyin: bù. Standard negation for present/future/habitual verbs and adjectives; shifts to bú before a 4th tone (不是 bú shì).

examples.text: 下雨的时候，纸不会弄丢房间名单。
examples.trans: When it rains, paper will not lose the room list.

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

meanings.note: Pinyin: bù shǎo. Litotes literally meaning 'not few', i.e. 'quite a lot of / plenty of'.

examples.text: 星期六早上有不少邻居来买热面包。
examples.trans: Quite a few neighbours come to buy warm bread on Saturday morning.

examples.text: 打折以后，我们省下了不少零钱。
examples.trans: After the discount, we saved plenty of spare change.

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎng. Used instead of 二 when counting things with a measure word (两个, 两把, 两间).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gè. Most common Mandarin measure word (量词), placed between a number/demonstrative and a noun (一个人, 这个).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yě. Always stands directly before the verb or adjective, never at the end of a clause.

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 周经理早！桌子很干净，钥匙也准备好了。
examples.trans: Morning, Manager Zhou! The desk is clean, and the keys are ready too.

meanings.note: Pinyin: mǎi. Everyday verb for purchasing goods; contrasts in tone with 卖 (mài 'sell').

examples.text: 看我的！快说要买什么。
examples.trans: Watch me! Tell me quickly what to buy.

examples.text: 九分钟！牛奶、鸡蛋和苹果都买来了！
examples.trans: Nine minutes! The milk, eggs, and apples are all here!

meanings.note: Pinyin: le. After a verb, marks completion; at the end of a sentence, signals a change of situation.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: Pinyin: èr. Used in counting, ordinals (第二), room numbers, and multi-digit numbers (二十); use 两 before measure words.

examples.text: 是的，宋老师，二楼四号房！坐火车累吗？
examples.trans: Yes, Teacher Song, room four on the second floor! Was the train ride tiring?

examples.text: 二十五年前我在附近教钢琴，不过记忆淡了。
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I taught piano nearby, though memories fade.

meanings.note: Pinyin: fù. Used for paying money or bills (付钱 'pay money').

examples.text: 付了现金！打开工具箱等我，我往桥那边跑回来了！
examples.trans: Paid in cash! Open your toolbox and wait—I am running back across the bridge!

examples.text: 我已经付过房租了。
examples.trans: I have already paid the rent.

meanings.note: Pinyin: huì. Expresses either an acquired skill (会弹钢琴) or likelihood in the future (会下雨).

examples.text: 下雨的时候，纸不会弄丢房间名单。
examples.trans: When it rains, paper will not lose the room list.

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nǐ. Everyday singular 'you' among colleagues, friends, and peers; use 您 for polite respect.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Qing, right? I am Mei from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nǐ men. Plural 'you' for addressing two or more people (including polite groups).

examples.text: 太谢谢你们两位了。
examples.trans: Thank you both so very much.

examples.text: 不怪你们。只是我身上只有这件外套！
examples.trans: It is not your fault. Still, I only have this one coat on me!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zuò. Everyday verb for preparing food, doing work, or making objects.

examples.text: 等等，咸黄油配果酱不行，做炒蛋却棒极了！
examples.trans: Wait—salted butter fails with jam, yet for scrambled eggs it is amazing!

examples.text: 小晴买了海盐黄油，今天我们做嫩炒蛋！
examples.trans: Qing bought sea-salt butter, so today we are making soft scrambled eggs!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiàng. Introduces a likeness or example ('look like, be like').

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

examples.text: 他长得真像他哥哥。
examples.trans: He really looks like his older brother.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gōng jīn. Standard metric weight classifier ('kilogram', equal to two 斤 jīn).

examples.text: 小美在水果摊买了三公斤黄柠檬。
examples.trans: Mei bought three kilos of yellow lemons at the fruit stall.

examples.text: 这个竹篮子最多能装五公斤水果。
examples.trans: This bamboo basket can hold at most five kilograms of fruit.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài. Marks a next step in sequence (先提再推) or a future repetition (再见 'see you again').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jǐ. Asks about small numbers (几点 'what time', 几个 'how many') before a measure word.

examples.text: 真的？您不介意多爬几步楼梯？
examples.trans: Really? You do not mind climbing a few extra stairs?

examples.text: 那家五金店早上几点开门？
examples.trans: What time does that hardware shop open in the morning?

meanings.note: Pinyin: dào. Works as main verb ('arrive') or result complement ('succeed in reaching/perceiving', 找到, 听到).

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房今天到。
examples.trans: Right, eight guest rooms, eight brass keys. Room four arrives today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qián mian. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 最前面 ('the very front').

examples.text: 前面锁扣有个小锁孔，再看底下贴着：一把旧铜钥匙！
examples.trans: There is a tiny keyhole on the front latch, and taped underneath: an old brass key!

examples.text: 前面路口往右拐就是火车站。
examples.trans: Turn right at the intersection ahead and you are at the station.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiā. Used for adding sugar, milk, or extra items (加糖 'add sugar').

examples.text: 请给我不加糖的红茶，再来一片热面包。
examples.trans: Black tea without added sugar, please, and one slice of warm bread.

examples.text: 太好了！请加牛奶和一点糖。
examples.trans: Wonderful! With milk and a little sugar, please.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sháo. Used both as a noun (勺子 'spoon') and as a measure word for spoonfuls (一勺蜂蜜 'a spoonful of honey').

examples.text: 喝热柠檬茶的时候，加一勺蜂蜜最香。
examples.trans: Hot lemon tea smells best when you add a spoonful of honey.

examples.text: 请给我拿一把干净的小木勺。
examples.trans: Please bring me a clean little wooden spoon.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shí. Cardinal number 10; building block for 11–99.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qù. Movement away from the speaker, as main verb (去车站) or directional complement (上去).

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 晚上九点？你站这儿，我们一起去开门。
examples.trans: Nine in the evening? Stay right here; let us go open the gate together.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yòu. Marks an action repeating, or pairs two qualities in 又A又B ('both A and B').

examples.text: 真的可以吗？看着又好看又暖和！
examples.trans: Is that really alright? It looks both lovely and warm!

examples.text: 又是深蓝色行李箱！这是宋老师的吗？
examples.trans: Another dark-blue suitcase! Is this Teacher Song's?

meanings.note: Pinyin: ba. At the end of a sentence, softens commands into friendly suggestions ('let's…') or asks for confirmation.

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Qing, right? I am Mei from the kitchen.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ne. After a noun, asks 'what about X?' (你呢？); at the end of a statement, highlights an ongoing situation.

examples.text: 等一下，咖啡厅的小美正朝我招手呢！
examples.trans: Wait a moment—Mei in the café is waving toward me right now!

examples.text: 来成都的第一个晚上，怎么能难过呢！
examples.trans: On your very first evening in Chengdu, how could you sit around sad!

meanings.note: Pinyin: hé. Joins nouns or pronouns ('A and B'), NEVER two whole clauses; also means 'with' (和你一样).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: la. Colloquial fusion of 了 + 啊 adding cheerful energy at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 你们守着，我出门啦！
examples.trans: Hold the fort—I am heading out the door!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài. As main verb/preposition, gives location (在院子里); before another verb, marks ongoing action ('be doing').

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dì fang. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个地方 ('a place').

examples.text: 等等——三楼楼梯上面是什么地方？
examples.trans: Wait—what is above the stairs on the third floor?

examples.text: 谢谢你们实话实说，没让我冒雨再找地方。
examples.trans: Thank you both for speaking honestly instead of sending me back into the rain.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dà. Everyday adjective for size, age, and strong wind or rain.

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 两双棕色大男鞋，还有灰色毛衣。
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes, plus grey sweaters.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tài. Often frames 太 + adj + 了 for warm exclamations (太好了！ 'Wonderful!').

examples.text: 太好了。请告诉我需要知道什么。
examples.trans: Great. Please tell me what I need to know.

examples.text: 太好了。窗户朝街上还是朝院子？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

meanings.note: Pinyin: hǎo. Main adjective 'good'; as a result complement after a verb, means 'ready/completed properly' (修好, 准备好).

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

meanings.note: Pinyin: mā ma. Everyday warm word for mother (second syllable neutral tone).

examples.text: 我妈妈做的柠檬果酱一点也不腻。
examples.trans: The lemon jam my mum makes is not cloying at all.

examples.text: 周末回家，我给妈妈带了一罐百花蜂蜜。
examples.trans: Going home for the weekend, I brought Mum a jar of wildflower honey.

meanings.note: Pinyin: cháng. Specifically tasting food or drink (尝一尝 / 尝一下); contrast 试 ('try out' objects or clothes).

examples.text: 快来尝一口刚出炉的热面包！
examples.trans: Come taste a bite of warm bread fresh from the oven!

examples.text: 卖蜂蜜的大姐请我们尝了一小勺山蜂蜜。
examples.trans: The honey vendor invited us to taste a little spoonful of mountain honey.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiù. Highlights immediacy, exact location (就在这里), or smooth consequence ('then').

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

examples.text: 朝院子，就在老树上面，非常安静。
examples.trans: Toward the courtyard, right above the old tree; it is very quiet.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shān. Measure word (量词): 座 (zuò), e.g. 一座山 ('a mountain').

examples.text: 这种深色蜂蜜是山里的蜂农送来的。
examples.trans: This dark honey was brought in by beekeepers from the mountains.

examples.text: 雨停以后，远处的青山看得特别清楚。
examples.trans: After the rain stopped, the green hills in the distance looked crystal clear.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǐ jīng. Often pairs with sentence-final 了 (已经到了 'has already arrived').

examples.text: 没错！你已经很习惯这儿了。
examples.trans: Exactly! You already fit right in here.

examples.text: 还好烤箱里的面团已经准备好了。
examples.trans: Thankfully the bread dough in the oven is already ready.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dài lù. Separable verb-object compound 带 ('lead') + 路 ('way/road').

examples.text: 志鹏熟悉这片老街，让他在前面带路吧。
examples.trans: Peng knows these old streets well—let him lead the way in front.

examples.text: 谢谢你带路，不然我们肯定找不到这家小店。
examples.trans: Thank you for leading the way, or we never would have found this little shop.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bāng máng. Separable verb-object compound (帮个忙 'do a favor').

examples.text: 我们替他看管了一周蓝箱子，他一定愿意帮忙！
examples.trans: After we guarded his blue suitcase all week, he will gladly help!

examples.text: 行李箱太重了，让我来帮忙吧。
examples.trans: That suitcase is heavy—let me give you a hand.

meanings.note: Pinyin: guáng chǎng. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个广场 ('a public square').

examples.text: 再往左拐进小广场，找一扇蓝木门。
examples.trans: Then turn left into the small square and look for a blue wooden door.

examples.text: 早上有不少老人在小广场散步。
examples.trans: Plenty of seniors stroll around the small square in the morning.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hěn. Links a subject to a simple predicate adjective without needing 是 (今天很冷 'It is cold today').

examples.text: 你好，小美，很高兴认识你！好香啊！
examples.trans: Hello, Mei, nice to meet you! Something smells wonderful!

examples.text: 没错！你已经很习惯这儿了。
examples.trans: Exactly! You already fit right in here.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kuài. As an adjective/adverb, 'fast/quickly'; in 快…了, 'about to'.

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 小晴，快看里面！这不是我的箱子！
examples.trans: Qing, look inside quickly! This is not my case!

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ. First-person singular pronoun; add 的 for 'my' (我的) and 们 for 'we/us' (我们).

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ men. First-person plural pronoun; add 的 for 'our' (我们的).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǎo. Focuses on searching; add 到 (找到) for actually finding.

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

examples.text: 我正在打……您好，请问有人找蓝色行李箱吗？
examples.trans: I am calling now... Hello, excuse me, is anyone looking for a blue suitcase?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǎo huí. Compound 找 ('give change / look for') + 回 ('back'); used for coins/notes returned after paying cash.

examples.text: 我付了五十块现金，老板找回六个硬币。
examples.trans: I paid fifty yuan in cash and the vendor gave back six coins in change.

examples.text: 小晴在坐垫下面找回了丢失的铜钥匙。
examples.trans: Qing recovered the missing brass key from underneath the seat cushion.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ná. Core verb for holding or fetching objects in the hand.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

examples.text: 火车站有人拿错了我的蓝色行李箱！
examples.trans: Someone at the train station took my blue suitcase by mistake!

related.gloss: handle with care (lift gently, set down gently)

meanings.en: lift up; carry (by a handle); mention
meanings.note: Pinyin: tí. Used for lifting a door handle or carrying a bag by its strap/handle.

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 从这儿往里走。我帮您把蓝色行李箱提上去。
examples.trans: Walk inward from here. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tān. Open-air market table or vendor stall (水果摊 'fruit stall', 陶瓷摊 'pottery stall'). Measure word: 个 (gè).

examples.text: 星期六广场上摆满了卖鲜花和水果的小摊。
examples.trans: On Saturdays, the square is lined with stalls selling fresh flowers and fruit.

examples.text: 转角那个陶瓷摊的茶杯又厚又好看。
examples.trans: The teacups at that pottery stall on the corner are both thick and handsome.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zǎo shang. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个早上 ('a morning').

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī wǔ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 每个星期五 ('every Friday').

examples.text: 我念念：对不起拿错了，请帮我保管到星期五。
examples.trans: Let me read it: Sorry for taking the wrong one; please keep mine until Friday.

examples.text: 到星期五？没写名字，也没签名！
examples.trans: Until Friday? No name written, and no signature either!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī liù. Literally 'week-day six'; Mainland standard alongside informal 周六 (zhōu liù).

examples.text: 每个星期六早上，这条老街都有热闹的集市。
examples.trans: Every Saturday morning, this old street hosts a lively market.

examples.text: 星期六下午来院子里喝杯热柠檬茶吧。
examples.trans: Come to the courtyard for a cup of hot lemon tea on Saturday afternoon.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nuǎn. Describes cozy warmth of tea, sunlight, or clothing.

examples.text: 每次弹完琴，他都问为什么下雨天钢琴声音更暖。
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, he asked why the piano sounded warmer on rainy days.

examples.text: 喝碗热汤，身子一下子就暖了。
examples.trans: Drink a bowl of hot soup and you warm right up.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gèng. Placed before an adjective or mental verb to form a comparative ('even better' 更好).

examples.text: 每次弹完琴，他都问为什么下雨天钢琴声音更暖。
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, he asked why the piano sounded warmer on rainy days.

examples.text: 生活安排的二重奏比我们自己写得更妙，孩子们。
examples.trans: Life arranges finer duets than we write ourselves, boys.

条.gloss: measure word for streets, rivers, towels, clauses

meanings.en: measure word for streets, rivers, towels, clauses
meanings.note: Pinyin: tiáo. Counts long, narrow, or winding things: streets, rivers, scarves, towels, trousers, and legal clauses (一条街).

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: níng méng. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个柠檬 ('a lemon').

examples.text: 他爷爷会切热柠檬蛋糕，上面撒一层白糖粉！
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with a dusting of powdered sugar on top!

examples.text: 啊！黄色柠檬糖霜——每个星期五我们俩都抢边角那一块！
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze—every single Friday the two of us fought over the corner piece!

meanings.note: Pinyin: níng méng tǎ. Compound 柠檬 ('lemon') + 塔 ('tart', phonetic loan). Measure word: 个 (gè) or 块 (kuài).

examples.text: 小美用新鲜黄柠檬烤了一盘香喷喷的柠檬塔。
examples.trans: Mei baked a fragrant tray of lemon tarts with fresh yellow lemons.

examples.text: 酸酸甜甜的柠檬塔最适合配热红茶。
examples.trans: Sweet-and-tangy lemon tarts pair best with hot black tea.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bǐ. Forms comparisons in A 比 B + adj ('A is more adj than B').

examples.text: 说实话，我比以前灰色办公室喜欢这儿多了。
examples.trans: Honestly, I like this place far better than my old grey office.

examples.text: 听听他说的！老陈比我们好奇两倍！
examples.trans: Listen to him! Chen is twice as curious as we are!

meanings.en: not have; there is not; did not
meanings.note: Pinyin: méi yǒu. Negates 有 ('have / there is') and past actions.

examples.text: 可惜没有电话号码，只有两个字母和老街名字。
examples.trans: Unfortunately there is no phone number, only two letters and an old street name.

examples.text: 还没有吗？请记下我们客栈的电话和地址，谢谢！
examples.trans: Not yet? Please write down our inn's phone number and address, thank you!

meanings.note: Pinyin: nóng. Describes rich honey, strong tea/coffee, or deep fragrance; opposite of 淡 (dàn, 'light/mild').

examples.text: 这种深色山蜂蜜花香很浓，泡茶只要半勺。
examples.trans: This dark mountain honey has a rich floral aroma—half a spoonful is enough for tea.

examples.text: 爷爷早上喜欢喝一杯浓一点的热红茶。
examples.trans: Grandpa likes drinking a slightly stronger cup of hot black tea in the morning.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shēn sè. Built from 深 ('deep') + 色 ('color'); opposite of 浅色 ('light-colored').

examples.text: 一，二……哇！看这深色的亮木头！
examples.trans: One, two... wow! Look at this dark, shiny wood!

examples.text: 他喜欢穿深色的衣服。
examples.trans: He likes wearing dark clothes.

meanings.note: Pinyin: rè. Describes hot tea, hot water, or warm weather.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiàn jīn. Measure word (量词): 笔 (bǐ), e.g. 一笔现金 ('a sum of cash').

examples.text: 给我袋子和现金！路口市场七点开门。
examples.trans: Give me a bag and cash! The corner market opens at seven.

examples.text: 付了现金！打开工具箱等我，我往桥那边跑回来了！
examples.trans: Paid in cash! Open your toolbox and wait—I am running back across the bridge!

related.gloss: a sum of cash (measure word 笔)

meanings.note: Pinyin: bō li. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块玻璃 ('a pane of glass').

examples.text: 小晴，隔着玻璃看——他们俩在树下面对面站着呢！
examples.trans: Qing, look through the glass—the two of them are standing face to face under the tree!

examples.text: 擦干净玻璃窗以后，屋里亮多了。
examples.trans: After wiping the glass window clean, the room is much brighter.

related.gloss: a pane of glass (measure word 块)

meanings.note: Pinyin: tián. Describes sweet pastries, fruit, or tea with honey.

examples.text: 那是海盐咸黄油！甜果酱面包卷要无盐黄油！
examples.trans: That is sea-salt butter! Sweet jam rolls need unsalted butter!

examples.text: 咸黄油能配甜草莓果酱吗？
examples.trans: Can salted butter go with sweet strawberry jam?

meanings.note: Pinyin: bái. Describes white paper, sugar, or tablecloths.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

examples.text: 看，把手上贴着一个白信封。
examples.trans: Look, there is a white envelope taped onto the handle.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bǎi huā. Literally 'a hundred flowers'; standard name for multi-floral wildflower honey (百花蜂蜜).

examples.text: 春天采的百花蜂蜜颜色金黄，香气清甜。
examples.trans: Wildflower honey harvested in spring has a golden colour and a clean, sweet aroma.

examples.text: 四月暖和起来，院子里百花盛开。
examples.trans: Once April warms up, all kinds of flowers bloom across the courtyard.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Links modifiers or owners to nouns (我的书 'my book', 安静的院子 'quiet courtyard').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: pí. Measure word (量词): 张 (zhāng), e.g. 一张皮 ('a piece of leather').

examples.text: 等等——柜台上这本棕色小皮笔记本是谁的？
examples.trans: Wait—whose small brown leather notebook is this on the counter?

examples.text: 啊，我的皮笔记本！谢谢！我正到处找呢。
examples.trans: Oh, my leather notebook! Thank you! I was looking everywhere for it.

related.gloss: a piece of leather (measure word 张)

meanings.note: Pinyin: shěng qián. Separable verb-object compound 省 ('save/economize') + 钱 ('money').

examples.text: 早市的水果又新鲜又便宜，比去大超市省钱。
examples.trans: Fruit at the morning market is fresh and affordable, saving money compared with big supermarkets.

examples.text: 买一打茶杯有折扣，帮客栈省了不少钱。
examples.trans: Buying a dozen teacups came with a discount, saving the inn quite a bit of money.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yìng bì. Literally 'hard currency' (硬 + 币), contrasting with 纸币 ('banknotes'). Measure word: 枚 (méi) or 个 (gè).

examples.text: 零钱袋里装着十几个亮晶晶的一元硬币。
examples.trans: Inside the coin pouch are more than a dozen shiny one-yuan coins.

examples.text: 买报纸需要两枚硬币，正好我口袋里有。
examples.trans: Buying the newspaper takes two coins, and I happen to have them in my pocket.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lí. Frames distance between two places or times: A 离 B 很近 ('A is close to B').

examples.text: 把小木桌放在树下面吧，离门口远一点。
examples.trans: Let's put the small wooden table right under the tree, a little farther from the doorway.

examples.text: 客栈离火车站只有十分钟路。
examples.trans: The inn is only ten minutes away from the train station.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qiū tiān. Compound 秋 ('autumn') + 天 ('season/sky').

examples.text: 秋天的山蜂蜜味道最浓，颜色也偏深。
examples.trans: Mountain honey gathered in autumn has the richest flavour and a deeper amber colour.

examples.text: 成都的秋天凉快又舒服，最适合在院子里喝茶。
examples.trans: Autumn in Chengdu is cool and comfortable—ideal for drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǒng. Read zhǒng as a measure word for kinds/types (这种, 那种); read zhòng as the verb 'plant/grow'.

examples.text: 老陈，这些香草是你自己种的吗？
examples.trans: Chen, did you grow these herbs yourself?

examples.text: 老房子连着旧回忆——那种争吵最伤人。
examples.trans: Old houses are tied to old memories—arguments like that cut deepest.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhàn. As a verb, 'stand' (站在旁边); as a noun, 'station/stop' (火车站).

examples.text: 晚上九点？你站这儿，我们一起去开门。
examples.trans: Nine in the evening? Stay right here; let us go open the gate together.

examples.text: 听得很清楚。你站在小石头喷泉旁边吗？
examples.trans: Loud and clear. Are you standing beside the little stone fountain?

meanings.note: Pinyin: lán zi. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个篮子 ('a basket').

examples.text: 篮子里正躺着六个黄柠檬呢——厨房就等今天了！
examples.trans: Six yellow lemons are sitting in my basket right now—this kitchen was waiting for today!

examples.text: 竹篮子里装着刚烤好的热面包卷。
examples.trans: Freshly baked warm bread rolls sit inside the bamboo basket.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gěi. As main verb, 'give'; as preposition/complement, marks the recipient (给你 'for/to you', 递给我 'pass to me').

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

罐.gloss: jar of; pot of; tin of

meanings.en: jar of; pot of; tin of
meanings.note: Pinyin: guàn. Serves both as a noun (罐子 'jar/crock') and as a measure word for jars or tins (两罐蜂蜜 'two jars of honey').

examples.text: 竹篮子里装着两罐沉甸甸的百花蜂蜜。
examples.trans: Packed inside the bamboo basket are two heavy jars of wildflower honey.

examples.text: 小美做了四小罐草莓果酱放在厨房架子上。
examples.trans: Mei made four small jars of strawberry jam and set them on the kitchen shelf.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nì. Describes desserts or rich food that feel overly heavy or cloying; 一点也不腻 ('not cloying at all') is high praise!

examples.text: 这款蜂蜜柠檬塔酸甜适中，吃起来一点也不腻。
examples.trans: This honey-lemon tart balances sweet and tart, so it doesn't taste cloying at all.

examples.text: 油炸的点心吃多了容易觉得腻，配杯清茶正好。
examples.trans: Rich fried pastries can feel heavy if you eat too many—a cup of clear tea balances them nicely.

meanings.note: Pinyin: chá. Measure word (量词): 杯 (bēi), e.g. 一杯茶 ('a cup of tea').

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 先喝杯热茶，吃个肉桂卷坐十分钟吧！
examples.trans: Have a cup of hot tea and a cinnamon roll for ten minutes first!

related.gloss: a cup of tea (measure word 杯)

meanings.note: Pinyin: chá bēi. Measure word (量词): 只 (zhǐ), e.g. 一只茶杯 ('a teacup').

examples.text: 只有裙子、乐谱，还有我最喜欢的茶杯！
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite teacup!

examples.text: 里面的茶杯呢？还完好吗？
examples.trans: And the teacup inside? Is it still intact?

meanings.note: Pinyin: fēng mì. Measure word (量词): 勺, e.g. 一勺蜂蜜 ('a spoonful of honey').

examples.text: 宋老师，给您热薄荷茶和蜂蜜。
examples.trans: Teacher Song, here is hot mint tea and honey for you.

examples.text: 太明智了！旁边要配蜂蜜还是苹果果酱？
examples.trans: Wise choice! Would you like honey or apple jam on the side?

related.gloss: a spoonful of honey (measure word 勺)

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiē. Measure word (量词): 条 (tiáo), e.g. 一条街 ('a street').

examples.text: 可惜没有电话号码，只有两个字母和老街名字。
examples.trans: Unfortunately there is no phone number, only two letters and an old street name.

examples.text: 等等，这条街就在附近，走过去只要五分钟！
examples.trans: Wait—that street is right nearby, only five minutes on foot!

meanings.en: neighbors; folks on the same street
meanings.note: Pinyin: jiē fang. Measure word (量词): 位 (wèi), e.g. 一位街坊 ('a neighborhood resident').

examples.text: 超过八十年的小院建筑，只要一楼每天服务街坊邻居，禁止改成私人办公室。
examples.trans: Any courtyard building over eighty years old may not become private offices as long as the ground floor serves neighbours daily.

examples.text: 每天服务街坊邻居——就像对公众开放的早间咖啡馆？！
examples.trans: Serves neighbours daily—like a morning café open to the public?!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhuāng. Used for packing items into a bag/box (装进) or fitting hardware.

examples.text: 我来帮您。哎呀，里面装了石头吗？
examples.trans: Let me help you. Goodness, did you pack stones inside?

examples.text: 他没要回那个装木头小火车的箱子吗？
examples.trans: Did he not ask back for that case with the wooden train?

meanings.en: want; need; will / be going to
meanings.note: Pinyin: yào. Direct verb for ordering/requesting ('want'), obligation ('need to'), or imminent future (要下雨了).

examples.text: 今天四号房的客人住一整个星期，一定要完美！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week; everything must be perfect!

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiàn. Appears in farewells (再见, 明天见) and as result complement of perception (看见, 听见).

examples.text: 晚安，小晴。明天早餐见。
examples.trans: Good night, Qing. See you at breakfast tomorrow.

examples.text: 老陈，听得见吗？我刚经过绿药店！
examples.trans: Chen, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: gēn. As a verb, 'follow' (跟我来 'follow me'); as a preposition, 'with' (跟你一样 'same as yours').

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhuǎn jiǎo. Note 转 is read 3rd-tone zhuǎn ('change direction/turn a corner') here, not 4th-tone zhuàn ('spin in circles')!

examples.text: 往前走五十米，转角就是那家很有名的陶瓷摊。
examples.trans: Walk fifty metres ahead and the famous pottery stall is right at the corner.

examples.text: 梧桐巷转角新开了一家飘着麦香的面包房。
examples.trans: A bakery smelling of toasted wheat just opened on the corner of Wutong Lane.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hái. Everyday adverb meaning 'still' (还在), 'not yet' (还没), or 'even more' after 比.

examples.text: 还没有吗？请记下我们客栈的电话和地址，谢谢！
examples.trans: Not yet? Please write down our inn's phone number and address, thank you!

examples.text: 宋老师，真对不起，那边还没有消息。
examples.trans: Teacher Song, I am truly sorry; they have no news over there yet.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhè. Proximal demonstrative; pairs with a measure word before nouns (这个 'this one', 这间房 'this room').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhè me. Proximal degree adverb (这么快 'this fast', 这么重 'so heavy').

examples.text: 怪不得这么重，全是木头和皮鞋！
examples.trans: No wonder it was so heavy—all wood and leather shoes!

examples.text: 这么快就修好了？老陈你随身带着螺丝刀啊！
examples.trans: Fixed that fast? Chen, you carry a screwdriver everywhere on you!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhèr. Spoken variant of 这里 ('here').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 没错！你已经很习惯这儿了。
examples.trans: Exactly! You already fit right in here.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nà xiē. Plural of 那个 ('those').

examples.text: 老陈，抱起那些纸箱，我们下楼吧！
examples.trans: Chen, pick up those cardboard boxes—down the stairs we go!

examples.text: 抬头看夜空下那些金色灯笼——真宁静啊！
examples.trans: Look up at those golden lanterns against the night sky—how peaceful!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhòng. Describes heavy luggage, heavy tools, or serious matters.

examples.text: 很安静，谢谢，不过这个行李箱今天特别重。
examples.trans: Very quiet, thank you, though this suitcase feels especially heavy today.

examples.text: 怪不得这么重，全是木头和皮鞋！
examples.trans: No wonder it was so heavy—all wood and leather shoes!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǎng dà. Note 长 is read 3rd-tone zhǎng ('grow') here, not 2nd-tone cháng ('long')!

examples.text: 志鹏就在离星期六集市三条街的老院子里长大。
examples.trans: Peng grew up in an old courtyard three streets away from the Saturday market.

examples.text: 院子角落那棵小柠檬树慢慢长大了。
examples.trans: That little lemon tree in the corner of the courtyard has slowly grown up.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wén. Everyday verb for smelling aromas (闻到香味 'smell a fragrance').

examples.text: 早上好！在楼上就闻到暖暖的肉桂香味了！
examples.trans: Good morning! All the way upstairs I smelled warm cinnamon!

examples.text: 一进门就闻到了烤面包的香味。
examples.trans: Right on stepping inside, I smelled baking bread.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yáng guāng. Measure word (量词): 缕, e.g. 一缕阳光 ('a ray of sunlight').

examples.text: 趁着阳光亮，我能再看看那张小纸牌吗？
examples.trans: While the sunlight is bright, may I look at that small paper tag again?

examples.text: 雨过天晴，温暖的阳光洒满整个小院。
examples.trans: After the rain cleared, warm sunshine filled the whole courtyard.

related.gloss: a ray of sunlight (measure word 缕)

meanings.note: Pinyin: táo cí. Collective compound joining 陶 ('earthenware/stoneware') + 瓷 ('porcelain').

examples.text: 广场转角的陶瓷摊摆满了白碗、茶杯和花瓶。
examples.trans: The ceramics stall on the corner of the square is covered in white bowls, teacups, and vases.

examples.text: 包陶瓷餐具的时候一定要多垫几层旧报纸。
examples.trans: Always pad ceramic tableware with extra layers of old newspaper when wrapping it.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jí shì. Traditional open-air neighbourhood or farmers' market (星期六集市 'Saturday market').

examples.text: 星期六一早，小晴和小美提着竹篮去逛集市。
examples.trans: First thing Saturday morning, Qing and Mei carry bamboo baskets to browse the street market.

examples.text: 集市上的本地蜂蜜和黄柠檬比超市新鲜多了。
examples.trans: Local honey and yellow lemons at the street market are much fresher than in supermarkets.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǔ hòu. Measure word (量词): 场 (chǎng), e.g. 雨后清晨 ('a morning after rain').

examples.text: 小晴早！经理您好！雨后的早晨真晴朗。
examples.trans: Morning, Qing! Hello, Manager! How bright the morning is after the rain.

examples.text: 雨后的石板路干净得像洗过一样。
examples.trans: After the rain, the flagstones looked freshly washed.

related.gloss: a morning after rain (measure word 场)

meanings.note: Pinyin: yù suàn. Compound 预 ('in advance') + 算 ('calculate'): planned spending limit.

examples.text: 今天集市打折，买齐所有东西还比预算省了三十块！
examples.trans: With today's market discounts, buying everything on our list still came in thirty yuan under budget!

examples.text: 小晴把每一笔支出都清清楚楚地记在预算本上。
examples.trans: Qing recorded every single expense clearly in the budget notebook.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiāng. Puts warm praise on fragrant tea/bread and even deep, restful sleep (睡得香).

examples.text: 你好，小美，很高兴认识你！好香啊！
examples.trans: Hello, Mei, nice to meet you! Something smells wonderful!

examples.text: 这是我这个月睡得最香的一晚，洗澡水也热极了！
examples.trans: Best sleep I have had all month, and the shower water was wonderfully hot!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiāng cǎo. Measure word (量词): 盆, e.g. 一盆香草 ('a pot of herbs').

examples.text: 好。端上去之前，在上面撒这些新鲜绿香草。
examples.trans: Good. Before serving them, sprinkle these fresh green herbs on top.

examples.text: 老陈，这些香草是你自己种的吗？
examples.trans: Chen, did you grow these herbs yourself?

related.gloss: a pot of herbs (measure word 盆)
